title: Making Knowledge Distillation Cheap Enough to Run at Scale
summary: The article discusses advancements in making knowledge distillation—a technique to train smaller 'student' models to match the performance of larger 'teacher' models—more efficient and scalable. The authors introduce two key systems changes: offline distillation using cached top-K logits to eliminate the need for keeping the teacher model in memory, and a fused chunked KL-divergence loss to reduce memory usage significantly. These innovations enable long-context distillation on a single GPU, drastically cutting costs and making large-scale experimentation practical.
key_points: Knowledge distillation is a critical technique for compressing large language models (LLMs) but is traditionally expensive due to high VRAM requirements.

The standard online distillation method requires both teacher and student models to be loaded simultaneously, leading to massive memory and compute costs (e.g., ~250GB VRAM for a single iteration with a 120B-parameter model).
The proposed **offline distillation** method caches the teacher's top-K logits (e.g., top-100 tokens per position) once, eliminating the need to recompute or store the teacher model during training.
The **fused chunked KL loss** processes data in chunks, avoiding the creation of a full vocabulary-size × sequence-length matrix, which reduces memory usage by up to **15.6×** at 32K tokens.
These optimizations enable distillation on a **single GPU** (e.g., H200) instead of requiring multi-GPU setups, reducing costs and iteration time by **5×** in some cases.
Benchmark results show near-identical training loss between online and offline methods, confirming the efficiency gains do not compromise model quality.
The resulting 3.2B-parameter student model retains most of the accuracy of its 8B-parameter teacher (e.g., Llama 3.1 8B Instruct) on benchmarks like BoolQ, HellaSwag, and MMLU.
The implementation is open-sourced, allowing teams to apply these optimizations to their own distillation pipelines.
